prompt: We have one persistent GitHub Actions self-hosted runner service today. Can we set max-parallel to 8 so that this one runner executes eight CI jobs at once, while keeping each job isolated?
assertions: the response states that strategy.max-parallel limits matrix fan-out and does not add concurrency inside one persistent runner agent
capacity eight is modeled as eight separately configured and registered runner agents/services, subject to machine capacity
each agent gets a distinct configured directory and workspace rather than starting eight processes from one configured runner directory

derived_from: references/self-hosted-runner-fleets.md § Give every pool one owner
prompt: Standardize persistent Actions runners for three projects on one Ubuntu machine. We want all mutable CI data under the gh-runner account home, but setup, cache, Docker cleanup, and removal for one project must not touch the others.
assertions: the response gives each project its own pool beneath ~/actions-runners/<project>/ with distinct per-slot instance directories
runner names, route labels or groups, services, caches, Compose projects, builders, and cleanup selectors are project-qualified
GitHub runner-group or repository access is used as the repository eligibility boundary rather than treating labels as access control
cleanup uses exact ownership labels or exact documented native-label matches and preserves unlabeled and sibling-project resources
the response states that one shared Unix account and Docker daemon provide operational isolation, not a hostile-tenant security boundary

derived_from: references/self-hosted-runner-fleets.md § Model lifecycle as state transitions
prompt: Build the setup and force-replace lifecycle for a persistent systemd GitHub Actions runner pool. It must support preparing runners without starting them and survive reboot safely.
assertions: bootstrap installs services stopped and disabled until required hooks and environment controls are verified
skip-start leaves units disabled across reboot, and skip-hooks cannot be combined with an enabled or started service
force replacement stops and removes the old service, uses a distinct removal token to deregister the old agent, then configures the new registration
a partial lifecycle failure is reported with recoverable local and GitHub state rather than deleting broadly or continuing silently
